page.layout: One column of running text, with marginal notes in the right margin. Below the text: the catchword "Supe-" and the signature "Z 4". Running head "CAPVT XXXII." and page number 359 at the top.

main_text.p: Constituitur autem ex coxarum extremis anteriori parte coëuntibus.
Estque hoc multò latius ac capacius in mulieribus, quàm viris.
Quò magis autē deorsum tendunt, eò magis ac magis disjunguntur, ut vacuam sedem pudendis relinquant.
Os coxendicis est media coxę pars, angustior quidem, sed crassior extrinsecus, in magnum ac profundum sinum excisa.Os coxendicis.
Hic sinus dicitur Acetabulum, in quod immittitur longum & rotundum femoris caput.
Exurgit ex hujus sinus labris crassa & circularis cartilago augens acetabuli capacitatem.
main_text.head: SECTIO XI. DE FEMORE.Undecima sectio.
main_text.p: Femur est os pedis omnium maximum supra acetabulo coxendicis, infrà genu inarticulatum.Femur.
Femoris caput est Superius & Inferius: utrumq; ex appendicibus supra infraq; huic osi adnatis formatum.Crus.

page.notes: Marginal notes on the right are small and faded; "Duodeci-" and the note beginning "Femur." may be the first part of a longer note, partly lost. The "Crus." note sits beside the lines of the paragraph beginning "Femoris caput", but its exact position is uncertain. Long s has been written as plain s throughout (e.g. "Eft" as "Est", "fedem" as "sedem", "ofsi" as "osi"). The heading "Undecima sectio." is a marginal note with a capital V, changed to U as a vowel. The show-through text in the background is not transcribed.
